51589143.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human GPER assessed as dissociation constant by SPR method

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis for Validation of GPER as a: SPR analysis was conducted using a Biacore T200 instrument (Cytiva). GPER protein was immobilized on a CM7 sensor chip (Cytiva) via the amine-coupling method, following standard protocols, in flow cell 2, while flow cell 1 served as a blank and was activated and deactivated. The immobilization procedure adhered to the manufacturer’s recommendations. GPER protein at a concentration of 200 μg/mL was diluted in a 10 mM acetate buffer (pH 4.0). For kinetic analysis, solutions of 6-26 with increasing concentrations (0–50 nM) were injected into two channels in SPR running buffer (HBS-EP+, 10 mM HEPES, 0.15 M NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.05% (v/v) Surfactant P20, pH 7.4) at a flow rate of 5 μL/min at 25 °C. Data were double-referenced using both reference cell RU values and signals from zero concentration (0.5% DMSO), and sensorgrams were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. K_D values were calculated by using kinetics analysis (1:1 model) in the Biacore T200 evaluation software.
original_paragraph.Figure 10 caption: Figure 10. Binding analysis by SPR sensorgram of 6-26. A series of concentrations are shown in different colors. Black lines are fitted curves from kinetic fitting using a 1:1 binding model. The Biacore T200 Evaluation Software was used to determine both k_d (dissociation constant) and k_a (association constant) values. The K_D (equilibrium constant) values were subsequently calculated from the obtained k_d and k_a values.

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: HBS-EP+, 10 mM HEPES, 0.15 M NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.05% (v/v) Surfactant P20, pH 7.4

data_analysis.reference_description: Flow cell 1 (blank), activated and deactivated; also zero concentration (0.5% DMSO) used for reference
